title: Android TabWidget: custom strips
purpose: Check that Android XML left and right strip drawables sit on either side of the selected tab.
changes: Added support for solid rectangular tabStripLeft and tabStripRight drawables, including @null and tabStripEnabled. The example uses a red left strip and blue right strip.
steps: Tap Second. A red strip should appear below First, and a blue strip should appear below Third, leaving the selected Second tab between them.
Tap First and Third in turn. The strips should move with the selected tab; a strip can be outside the widget when selection is at an edge.
Turn on Right-to-left layout and repeat. The order of the tabs reverses, and the strips still surround the selected tab.
Choose OK if it behaves as described, or Reject with details and your device.
expected: The red left and blue right strips extend from the selected tab toward their respective edges, and update when the tab or layout direction changes.
limits: This test uses solid rectangular drawables. Android theme drawables, drawable selectors, bitmaps and device pixel parity remain unsupported or unverified.

references.scope: Left and right strip bounds and drawing order.

validation: 155 XML importer tests and six TabWidget Rust tests passed, including null, disabled and RTL cases.
A 320 × 440 browser pixel test checked strip colors and RTL tab order.
